recipes.name: Seven Layer Party Dip
ingredients_raw: 4 cups shredded Cheddar-Monterey Jack cheese blend

steps.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir ground beef in the hot skillet until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Drain and set aside to cool to room temperature.

Spread beans on the bottom of a 9x13-inch glass dish or a serving platter. Sprinkle 2 cups of shredded cheese on top of beans. Spoon beef on top of cheese. Spread sour cream carefully on top of beef. Spread guacamole on top of sour cream. Pour salsa over guacamole and spread evenly. Sprinkle with remaining 2 cups shredded cheese. Sprinkle black olives, tomatoes, and green onions on top.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate overnight and serve cold.

raw_recipe.headline: Seven Layer Party Dip
raw_recipe.description: This 7-layer dip with meat, refried beans, guacamole, salsa, cheese, and olives is a great party dip because it's best served at room temperature.

review.reviewBody: Everyone loved this, but we all agreed it needed to be WAY more spicy. I substituted cream cheese for half of the sour cream, used a packet of taco seasoning in the beef, and another packet in the sour cream / cream cheese mixture. A half cup or so of canned sliced jalapenos as layer #8 makes this a lot better. If you like guacamole, use about twice as much, because the recommended amount isn't enough to even spread out to make a whole layer. You wouldn't notice if you left it out. I'll make this one again; it's very good.

I've used this recipe before and added more spices to the meat for extra flavor. Try adding 1 tbs red chili powder, 1 diced garlic clove, 1/2 yellow onion diced, and 1 tsp. Adobo seasoning. I usually re-fry the beans in a skillet because it makes them easier to spread. If you are feeling really adventurous make a fresh pot of "dirty beans" the day before and re-fry them to use in this recipe.

Turned out delicious! I added taco seasoning to the ground beef, a 1/2 tbsp. Johnny's Seasoning to two cups mashed avocado (instead of one avocado) for the guacamole layer; and instead of the tomato topping I used my homemade super spicy pico de gallo topping (one of my husbands favorites)! I made an extra large batch, and it vanished!

I added homemade taco seasoning and a small can of V-8 instead of water to the ground beef to give it some flavor. I also folded in one small can of mild green chilies to the refried beans. The boys loved it, GREAT for Superbowl Sunday.

Great recipe! It's a crowd favorite!

I had to modify it a little to appease my picky eaters. Instead of salsa, I used enchilada sauce. I also added salt, garlic and onion to the ground beef to intensify the flavor.

Also, before topping it with the tomatoes, green onions and olives, I toss it under the broiler for a couple minutes to melt the cheese.

As is, this recipe was not that great but it is a great base for a great recipe! The way I now make this dip is as follows:
I make the beef as if I were making regular tacos, I "drain" some of the salsa "juice" into the sour cream and mix it together so it's not just tartness. I throw it under the broiler for 5minutes, then I top it with lettuce, tomatoes, and olives and leave out the green onions since I hate them. I used Kraft shredded mexican cheese blend, and old el paso fat free spicy refried beans. I like a bit of spice and this way was a good balance of spicy without overpoweringly hot. Do like Taco Bell - Let Sour Cream sit out for a few minutes to soften (Not room temp just 5 minutes or so) then put it in a pastry/zip bag and squeeze it out for easy spreading!

Left out the meat. Instead of salsa I added a drained can of RoTel's tomato's with green Chiles to the beans with garlic salt. Guac with lemon and lime juices, salt, and I topped with added cilantro. So good.

This recipe turned out great. I made it for a going away party for my boss. I tweaked just a tad because I was lazy and didn't have time to defrost chopped meat plus I could find black olives in the store. Nevertheless my co-workers LOVED it! everyone went back for second and thirds. I will definitely make it again. In fact knowing my co-workers; it will be requested. So here's what I changed: instead of using hamburger meat I used black beans. I used that as my first layer. I drained the tomatoes as everyone's suggested before adding them to the dish. Also, my fourth 5 th layer I used canned corn. I kept the sour cream and guacamole separate to add more color and layers. I sprinkled the taco seasoning and some Adabo every third layer. No one noticed that there was no beef. They don't even mind. I feel the thickness of the beans helped with that. 

Two thumbs up!

To me, this recipe needs something else to give it more flavor and "depth." I thought it was a bit bland when made as directed. Update: Today I made this again but with a few additions which did the trick for us. Though this recipe is not designed to be a "taco" dip, it really does need something more. Therefore, like many other reviewers, I added a pkt of Taco Seasoning mix (no water) & 1 tsp of garlic bits to the ground meat as I browned it. I kept everything else the same (except omitted guacamole since we don't like it) and then baked it for 30 minutes at 350 degrees. It was great served warm with Frito Scoops! I think the secret ingredient (besides the taco mix) is the blend of Cheddar and Jack cheeses. This dish makes a "pretty" presentation for the table. BTW, if you do add Taco seasoning, do not add salt. It will be too salty for most people. Thanks DPerez7 for the recipe.

Had this many times at parties but this was my first time making it myself and it turned out fabulous. I used ingredients that I had in the fridge. For the first cheese layer I used a combination of shredded Mexican blend, a slice of diced American and diced jalapeño jack. Didn’t have sour cream so combined plain Greek yogurt with some cream cheese for that layer. Used shredded extra sharp cheddar for second cheese layer. Didn’t have green onions or olives so just used some finely chopped lettuce and lastly it looked like it had enough tomate with salsa so

Great recipe, with lots of room to customize! To amp up the flavor, I added a packet of spicy taco seasoning to the beef (you could use regular or mild as well). I also put the cheese on as the last layer and popped it under the broiler for a few minutes to melt. Delicious, and now everyone asks me to bring this to parties!
I think they forgot the taco seasoning, we used to sprinkle it over the sour cream layer.
I added taco seasoning 1pack Half pack in meat and the other half mixed into beans
Took this to a small gathering and it was gone as soon as the 1st person began raving at how delicious this was. I appreciate the post!!
It's really good. But, the title of the recipe is wrong. It's not 7 layer dip. It's actually 9 layer dip...

I loved it. I made a few changes. I used Pico de Giao instead of salsa, added mushrooms. Mixed cream cheese with sour cream and taco season. Used refried black beans instead of regular refried beans. Fritos Scoops...VOILA!!

Only 4 starts since it's not served hot.
My mom made this for me when I was young, she served this for Super Bowl.
She'd assemble this and put in a 350F oven for 30-40 minutes so it was nice & hot and cheese all melted.
I don't think I'd want it 'room temperature,
tyvm.
Great recipe!! I opted not to use ground meat & did a light layer of cilantro instead but I've made it a few times & it's always delicious.
Not a fan of guac, otherwise, excellent!!

This is by FAR my favorite dip recipe EVER. I added taco seasoning to the beef and whenever I make this for a gathering, everyone LOVES it. I have shared this recipe SO many times. Thank you D. Perez!!!
